Mounted Huscarls of a Norscan jarl's household, armoured in mail and bearing the broad shields of the longhall.

When a jarl rides to war, the best of his Huscarls ride beside him. Chosen from the hardest fighters of the hall and bound to their lord by oath and gold, they do not harry and skirmish like the Marauder Horsemen of the tribes. They strike as one, crash into the enemy flank behind a wall of shields and stay there, cutting down the foot soldiers who break before them.
Mounted Huscarls armed with heavy spears, the household riders a jarl sends against beasts, monsters and enemy cavalry.

Norsca breeds monsters as readily as men, and a jarl who cannot face both does not rule for long. His spear-armed Huscarls are trained to meet the charge of trolls, giants and armoured knights, setting their spears and their shields together so that the largest foe impales itself upon them. Well armoured and fiercely loyal, they are as much a bodyguard as a weapon.
Huscarls sworn upon their jarl's oath-ring, who will not leave the field while he still stands.

Among the northern tribes an oath sworn upon the temple ring binds a warrior until death and, the skalds say, beyond it. The Ring-Sworn are Huscarls who have given that oath to their jarl in front of the gods and the hall. They ride with spears and shields like their kin, yet they fight with the stubbornness of men who have already promised their lives, and in the press of melee they grow harder to break with every blow they trade.
